subject: Packaging enquiry
body:
Hi there,

Hope you're well. I came across Shellworks a while back and have been meaning to reach out properly.

We're a skincare brand based out of Denver, been going about four years now. Our hero product is a 60ml serum in a PP jar and honestly the jar has become a bit of a sticking point — one of our retail partners has started asking us fairly pointed questions about our packaging roadmap and we don't have a great answer right now. We're doing somewhere around 180k units a year on that SKU, a bit more if you count the travel size.

Ideally we'd want to make a change for our SS27 line which means deciding in the next couple of months I think.

Would you be able to send over technical info, and is it possible to get samples? Happy to send our current spec if that helps.

Thanks,

Maren Voss
Head of Operations
Lumen Botanicals

subject: Hello
body:
Hello,

Hope this finds you well. My name is Priya and I head up ops at Terra Nine — we do daily supplement capsules, mostly DTC with a bit of retail.

We're going through a rebrand at the moment and packaging is part of that conversation. Currently everything is in PET and it doesn't sit well with where the brand is going. We ship roughly 250k units a year across our two main SKUs.

A few things I'd want to understand before taking it further — what your minimum order looks like, lead times, and whether there's anything about the material that would cause problems for us on the filling side. We're funded through next year so this is a real project, not just exploratory.

Let me know who's best to speak to.

Best,
Priya Raghunathan
Head of Operations, Terra Nine
+1 (415) 555-0182

subject: Enquiry
body:
[Submitted via theshellworks.com contact form]

Name: Tom Ashworth
Company: Wildroot Co
Message: Hi! Big fan of what you guys are doing. I'm launching a magnesium supplement brand early next year and packaging is the thing I care most about getting right — I don't want to launch in plastic, it would undercut the whole thing.

First run would be small, maybe 2,000 units, just to see if there's demand. Still raising a small round but hoping to close in the next few months.

What sort of cost would I be looking at? And do you work with brands at this stage or should I come back when we're bigger?

Thanks
Tom

subject: Introduction
body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Good morning and I hope you are well.

Allow me to introduce our company. Promold Ibérica is an injection moulding group based in Catalonia, we operate 40 machines across two sites and we serve principally cosmetics and personal care clients in Spain, Portugal and the south of France. Some of our clients you would know.

The reason for my message is that increasingly our clients ask us for compostable options and at the moment we cannot offer anything credible. We have followed your material for some time. We would be interested to discuss whether we could process your material under some form of licence or supply arrangement for these clients.

To give you an idea of scale, across the clients who have raised this with us we would be speaking about several million units annually, though of course this would develop over time.

Would it be possible to arrange a call? I am available most of September.

With best regards,

Elena Ferrán
Commercial Director
Promold Ibérica S.L.
Tel: +34 93 555 0140

subject: Following up from K
body:
Hi,

We met briefly at K last year — I don't know if you'll remember, it was a busy few days.

Reason I'm getting in touch is we've got new twin-screw capacity coming online in Q1 and I remembered you mentioning you were looking at bringing more compounding in-house. Thought it was worth a note in case there's something we could support you with, either as overflow or for development runs.

Happy to send our spec sheet over if it's of interest.

All the best,
Gunnar Holm
Business Development
Nord Extrusion AS

subject: Thesis research
body:
Dear Shellworks team,

I hope you are doing well.

My name is Sofie and I am a master's student in Industrial Design Engineering at TU Delft. I am writing my thesis on the barriers to adoption of biopolymers in the cosmetics sector, looking specifically at why brands who say they want to switch often don't.

I would be very grateful if someone at Shellworks could spare 30 minutes for an interview. I am of course happy to share my findings with you once the thesis is complete, and I can work around whatever timing suits.

Thank you very much for considering,

Kind regards,
Sofie Bakker
MSc Industrial Design Engineering
TU Delft

subject: Quick question
body:
Hi,

Rob here from Packaging Europe. Hope all's well with you.

We're putting together a piece on how PPWR implementation is actually landing for the companies who make the alternative materials — as opposed to the brands — and I'd really like to get Insiya's view in there. It's shaping up to be a decent read, we've got a couple of the bigger names in already.

I need it by Friday afternoon unfortunately. Fifteen minutes on a call would do it, or I can send questions over by email if that's easier.

Cheers,
Rob Vincent
Senior Editor, Packaging Europe

subject: Bags
body:
Hello,

I hope you can help. I run a small pet supplies shop and I'm trying to find compostable poo bags that actually break down properly — I've been let down by two suppliers now who said theirs were compostable and they clearly weren't.

Do you make these? I'd be looking at maybe 500 boxes to start with and more if they sell.

Thanks very much,
Denise

subject: Order
body:
Hi,

Saw your chopping board on Instagram the other day and wanted to order one for my sister's birthday, but I can't find it anywhere on your website. Is it still available? Her birthday is the 14th so I'd need it fairly quickly, happy to pay extra for postage.

Thanks
Andrew

Sent from my iPhone

subject: Introduction
body:
Hi,

Hope you're having a good week.

I wanted to introduce myself — I work with high-growth materials and advanced manufacturing businesses on senior commercial appointments. We placed the VP Sales at two companies in adjacent spaces to yours last year and know the talent pool well.

I appreciate you may already have arrangements in place, but would you be open to a short call about your hiring plans over the next twelve months? Even if nothing's live right now it's useful to have the relationship.

Best wishes,
Charlotte Meakin
Partner, Apex Search Partners

subject: Northlight Growth
body:
Hi Insiya,

Hope you're well and that the summer treated you kindly.

I'm on the investment team at Northlight, we're a growth fund focused on industrial decarbonisation — cheque sizes typically Series B and beyond. We've been following Shellworks since your A and the ingredient-brand angle is one of the more interesting positions we've seen in materials.

No agenda here beyond opening a dialogue well ahead of any process. Would you be up for an intro call in September? Entirely happy for it to be informal.

Best,
Jonas Lindqvist
Northlight Growth Partners

subject: Specs
body:
Hi

Can you send over your material specs and any food contact documentation you have.

Thanks

Sent from my iPhone

subject: Enquiry on behalf of a client
body:
Good afternoon,

I hope this reaches the right person — apologies if not, do point me elsewhere.

I'm advising a large food and beverage business on packaging alternatives for one of their categories which is being reformulated. I'm not in a position to name them until we have an NDA in place, which I appreciate is a slightly awkward way to start a conversation.

What I can say is that the evaluation is funded, it's being run out of their group function rather than a single brand team, and they are working to a timeline.

Would you be open to getting a mutual NDA moving this week so we can have a proper conversation?

Regards,

Marcus Reiter
Haldane Partners

subject: Question
body:
Hi folks,

Hope you're well. Found you through a supplier list one of our customers sent over.

Quick bit of background — we're a private label manufacturer of frozen ready meals, we produce for two of the national grocery chains here in the US. Both of them have been leaning on us hard about plastic in the last eighteen months and frankly we're running out of road. We go through somewhere north of 4 million trays a year so it's not a small problem for us.

What I need to know before we go any further is whether your material can actually handle what we'd put it through. Trays sit at -18°C in distribution and then the consumer puts them in the microwave. If the answer's no, no hard feelings, but if it's yes I'd want to move on this quickly.

Appreciate any steer.

Wes Trent
Director of Procurement
Harbor Foods Group

subject: Hi!
body:
Hi both,

Hope you don't mind the cold email.

I'm a chef and I've just launched a small range of pantry products — pastes, oils, that sort of thing. I know I'm going to be far too small for you, we're doing about 8,000 units a year at the moment, so do feel free to say no.

The reason I'm asking anyway is that we're stocked in Selfridges and Fortnum's and there's a reasonable amount of press coming in the autumn, including a couple of the weekend supplements. Packaging is going to get talked about because it's part of the story I'm telling.

Is there any version of this that works for you at our size? Totally understand if not.

Nell

Nell Farrow
Founder, The Farrow Kitchen

subject: Information request
body:
Hi there,

Hope you're well.

We're at the very start of thinking about a packaging refresh planned for 2028 and I've been asked to gather information on what's out there. I want to be upfront that there's no budget allocated and no immediate timeline — I'd rather tell you that now than waste anyone's time.

That said, I'd genuinely like to understand what's possible so that when the conversation does get serious internally I know what I'm talking about. Do you have any kind of general information pack, or a webinar or similar?

Thanks,
Hannah Oduya
Packaging Development Manager
Brightleaf Wellness

subject: Enquiry
body:
Hello,

I hope you are well.

I am working on a refillable format for a new line we are launching next year and I am currently comparing suppliers for the cap component. The volume would be in the region of 90,000 pieces per year to begin with, likely growing.

I have looked at your website and the material seems interesting for this application, though I would want to understand the wear characteristics given it is a component that gets opened and closed repeatedly.

I should mention that I need to submit my comparison to our category director on Thursday, so if you are able to give me an indicative price before then I can include you. I realise this is short notice and I apologise for that.

Kind regards,

Camille Beaufort
Packaging Development
Maison Le Rêve

subject: Potential collaboration
body:
Dear Insiya,

I hope this email finds you well.

I lead a research group at Bath working on enzymatic degradation pathways for polyesters. We are putting together a consortium for an Innovate UK call which closes in November, and the bid is considerably stronger with an industrial partner attached — reviewers weight it heavily.

There would be matched funding involved and the work would be genuinely relevant to you rather than the sort of academic exercise that produces a paper and nothing else. I'd need to know fairly soon as the paperwork takes a while.

Would Shellworks be interested in a conversation?

With best wishes,

Prof. Alan Sturgess
Department of Chemical Engineering
University of Bath

subject: PHA supply
body:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Greetings and I hope you are keeping well.

We represent a fermentation producer in Southeast Asia who have brought new PHA capacity online this year and are looking to build relationships in Europe. Based on what we understand of European pricing at the moment we believe we could offer grades at a meaningful discount, though naturally that depends on volumes and specification.

Would you be open to receiving samples and an indicative price list? We can also arrange a technical call with the production team if useful.

Warm regards,
Ravi Chandran
Meridian Polymers Pte Ltd
Singapore

subject: Following up
body:
Hi,

I sent the below on the 10th and haven't heard anything so I'm assuming it went astray somewhere.

Original message: We're a contract manufacturer working with four supplement brands out of our facility in Leicester. Between them we're looking at somewhere around 400,000 units a year across jars and scoops, and two of the four have specifically asked whether we can offer a compostable option. At the moment we can't, which is starting to be a problem for us.

I'd like to understand what a supply relationship would look like and whether you'd work with us as the manufacturer rather than going direct to the brands.

I'll be honest, if I don't hear back this time I'll assume it's not of interest and look elsewhere. No hard feelings either way.

Yusuf Adebayo
Operations Director
Stillwater Supply Co

subject: Introduction
body:
Hello,

I hope you're well.

I'm writing on behalf of Dana Whitfield, our VP of Packaging (copied here), who would like to set up an introductory call regarding lidding and closure components.

Dana has some availability across the next two weeks — would you be able to send over some times that work at your end and I'll get something in the diary?

Many thanks,

Bethany Cole
Executive Assistant to Dana Whitfield
Kestrel Foods

subject: Quick question re: Shellworks
body:
Hi there,

Hope you're having a great week!

I came across Shellworks recently and was genuinely impressed by your innovative approach to sustainable packaging solutions — what you're building is exactly the kind of thing the industry needs more of.

I work with category-leading brands to amplify their reach through data-driven growth strategies, and I think there could be some real synergy here given where you're at in your journey.

Would you be open to a brief 15-minute call this week or next to explore how we might work together?

Looking forward to connecting!

Best,
Kyle Brennan
Founder, GrowthScale Media

subject: Question about our last order
body:
Hi,

Hope you're well, sorry to bother you.

We started running batch 4471 through the line this morning and we're getting cracking on the jars at the capping stage — it's maybe one in forty, something like that, but it's enough that we've had to stop the line while we work out what's going on. Could be us, could be the material, we honestly don't know yet.

This is our second production run with you and the first one was fine, so I don't think it's something we're doing differently.

Is there someone I can speak to today? We've got a fill scheduled for Thursday that we're going to miss otherwise.

Thanks,
Rachel Okonjo
Production Manager
Verve Botanica
07700 900412

subject: Hello
body:
Hello,

I hope you're well.

I lead packaging sustainability for a UK grocery group and we're in the process of updating the requirements we set for our own-brand suppliers. Part of that work is understanding which alternative materials are genuinely available at commercial scale as opposed to still being at pilot stage, because there's not much point writing requirements that nobody can meet.

I should be clear that this isn't a purchasing conversation — we wouldn't be buying from you directly. But the requirements we set do determine what a few hundred suppliers go out and buy, so I thought it was worth a conversation.

Would someone be able to spare half an hour?

Best regards,
Fiona Marchetti
Head of Packaging Sustainability
Aldwych Retail Group

subject: Application
body:
Hello,

I hope you don't mind me writing speculatively.

I'm a process engineer with six years in polymer extrusion, currently at a large converter, and I've reached the point where I'd like to be doing something that matters rather than optimising throughput on packaging that ends up in a hole in the ground. I've followed Shellworks for a while.

I can't see anything advertised on your site at the moment but I thought I'd ask anyway. CV attached in case anything opens up.

Thanks for your time,
Daniel Iwu

subject: Podcast
body:
Hey,

Hope you're well!

I host a podcast where we interview founders working on genuinely hard physical problems — supply chains, materials, manufacturing, the unglamorous stuff. Our listeners are mostly operators and investors in climate hardware.

We'd love to have Insiya on. It's about 45 minutes, remote, and we handle all the editing and promotion. No prep needed beyond a quick pre-call.

Let me know if there's any interest and I'll send over some dates.

Tash Merrill
Host, Material World

subject: Quote
body:
[Submitted via theshellworks.com contact form]

Name: Greg Salter
Company: Northmoor Supplements
Message: Hi, could you quote for 15,000 units annually of a 120ml jar please. We're a small UK brand but growing steadily year on year and would want to start in Q1. Also interested to know whether there's a volume at which the pricing changes significantly, as we'd like to understand what we'd be growing into.

Thanks
Greg Salter, Director

subject: Enquiry
body:
Hi there,

Hope all's well.

We're a mid-size injection moulder in Ohio, mostly personal care and household. Two of our customers have come to us in the last few months asking specifically about your material by name, which is a first for us — usually these requests are generic.

I'd rather figure out how to serve that than watch the work go somewhere else. What does it take to become an approved processor for your material? I'm assuming there's some qualification process, training, maybe equipment implications.

Happy to get on a call whenever suits.

Brandon Hoyt
VP Operations
Keystone Molding Inc.

subject: Question about your material
body:
Hello,

I hope you can point me in the right direction.

One of our MRF operators has flagged that they're starting to see bio-based packaging turning up in the PET stream and we're trying to get ahead of what that means for us. I'm contacting a few of the material producers directly rather than relying on what's written about it online.

Two questions really: does your material need separating out, and is there anything on-pack or detectable that would let a sorting line identify it?

Any help appreciated.

Regards,
Lorna Petrie
Technical Manager
Claymoor Recycling

subject: SB 54
body:
Hi,

Hope you're well.

With SB 54 obligations tightening and similar schemes coming through in other states, we're working with producers to model their fee exposure and build the reporting infrastructure before the deadlines bite.

Given your customer base I imagine this comes up constantly in your sales conversations. Would there be interest in some form of partner arrangement where we support your customers on the compliance side?

Best,
Simon Achebe
EPR Navigator

subject: Packaging
body:
Hi,

Hope you're well.

We're a pet supplements brand — powders and chews, mostly online with some independent retail. Our main SKU is a 500ml jar with a scoop inside, and we're doing about 300k units a year across the range now.

Two of our retail accounts have raised packaging with us in the last quarter and we've got budget signed off to make a change this year rather than kicking it down the road again. Our co-packer is in Illinois so anything we do needs to work for them too.

Who should I be talking to?

Thanks
Kim Dalgleish
Head of Supply Chain, Barkwell Pet

subject: Invitation
body:
Dear Insiya,

I hope this message finds you well.

I am writing to invite you to speak on our materials innovation panel in Lisbon next March. We expect around 1,200 attendees, predominantly brand-side packaging and sustainability leads from across Europe.

I should be transparent that we do not pay speaker fees, though we cover travel and accommodation. The panel is 45 minutes and we would work with you on the framing.

I do hope you'll consider it.

With kind regards,
Aurélie Danton
Programme Director
SustainPack Summit

subject: Anfrage / Enquiry
body:
Hello,

I hope you are well, and apologies for writing in English if that is easier for you than German.

We are a contract filler based in Baden-Württemberg working primarily with cosmetics brands. In the last quarter three of our clients have independently asked us about compostable primary packaging, which is not something we have been able to answer well.

I would like to be in a position to offer them something. Combined the volumes across those three would be in the region of 600,000 units per year, though they are separate businesses and would each make their own decision.

I am not entirely sure whether I should be speaking to you on their behalf or introducing them to you directly — perhaps you can advise which you prefer.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen,
Nadia Fischer
Geschäftsführerin
AurumFill GmbH

subject: Hi
body:
Hi team,

Hope you're well over there.

We're a supplements brand based in Melbourne, doing around 220k units a year, and we're very keen on what you're doing — it's the first thing I've seen that doesn't feel like greenwashing.

The obvious question before we get excited: can you actually supply into Australia, and what does that do to landed cost versus what we're paying now? I'd rather know early if the answer is no.

Cheers,
Josh Tallis
Co-founder, Meridian Wellness

subject: Pellets
body:
Hello,

I hope you are well.

We develop products for marine and aquaculture applications and we are interested in trialling your material on our own equipment before committing to anything.

Could you tell me what quantities you can supply in pellet form and what the price per kilo would be? We would start with something small, perhaps 50kg, and scale if the trials go well.

Best regards,
Dr Ingrid Solberg
Head of Product Development
Havlund Innovation AS

subject: Patent activity
body:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I hope you are well.

We monitor patent activity across bio-based polymers and have noted a number of recent filings in areas adjacent to what we understand Shellworks to be working on. Companies at your stage are often unaware of filings until they become a problem.

We offer a watch service tailored to growth-stage businesses. May I send over a sample report so you can see the sort of thing we produce?

Yours faithfully,
Peter Lund
Harrington IP

subject: Enquiry
body:
Hi,

Hope you're well.

We're looking at closures for our core range — around 500k units a year at the moment. I've read a fair bit about your material and I like the story a lot.

I'm going to be direct with you because I've wasted time on this before. Our finance team has already told me that anything more than about 15% over what we're currently paying for PP won't get approved, regardless of how good the sustainability case is. That's the constraint I'm working within and I don't have the political capital to change it this year.

If that's simply not workable at your end, I'd genuinely rather you told me now than after three months of samples and calls.

Best,
Alicia Ngata
Director of Product
Forma Haircare

subject: Partnership
body:
Hello,

I hope this finds you well.

We're a charity working on ocean plastics and we're looking for material partners for an awareness campaign launching next spring. The campaign will have significant reach — we're working with two broadcasters and had 40 million impressions on last year's equivalent.

I'll be upfront that we don't have budget on our side for this. What we can offer is association and reach, which for a company like yours seems like it could be valuable.

Would you be open to a conversation?

With thanks,
Douglas Bell
Partnerships Lead
OceanReach Trust

subject: Freight
body:
Dear Partner,

Good day and I hope you are well.

We are a freight forwarding company moving temperature-sensitive and industrial cargo throughout Europe and to North America. We can offer favourable rates on your Q4 volumes and are happy to quote against your existing arrangements to demonstrate the saving.

Please let me know if I may send our rate card.

Best regards,
Tomasz Wiśniewski
Key Account Manager
Baltic Trans Global

subject: Hello
body:
Hi,

Hope you're well.

We're a supplements brand doing around 200k units a year, mostly capsule jars. We've been looking at alternatives to our current packaging for a while and have narrowed it down to two options — you're one of them.

I want to be straightforward about where we are: our board has asked for this to be signed off before the quarter closes, so we're making a decision this month one way or the other. The other supplier has already sent samples.

What do you need from us to move quickly? I can get you whatever specs or volumes you need today.

Thanks,
Rebecca Cho
COO, Northstar Nutrition
